hero.subhead: The HR Toolkit Programme supports small and medium-sized enterprises from six selected regions of Moldova with practical HR tools, workshops and mentoring support.
hero.body2: The programme helps SMEs improve how they find, welcome, integrate and retain employees, especially young people.
hero.tagline: Better hiring. Better onboarding. Better retention.
hero.imageAlt: Business team collaborating in an office

why.heading: Why this programme
why.subheading: A good hire can fail if the first weeks are poorly managed
why.body1: Recruitment does not end when a candidate accepts the job. For many companies, the real challenge starts after hiring.
why.body2: A new employee may leave not because the job does not exist, but because expectations are unclear, the first working day is improvised, the supervisor is too busy, or feedback comes too late.
why.body3: The programme helps SMEs create simple and realistic practices that make the first days, weeks and months of employment more structured, supportive and effective.
why.peerBody: Connect with other SME leaders across Moldova

stat2.label: Programme regions
stat2.sub: Bălți · Chișinău · Edineț · Orhei · Soroca · Ungheni

pains.heading: Do these challenges sound
pains.subhead: These challenges are common across Moldova's small and medium-sized enterprises

item1.title: It is difficult to find suitable employees.
item1.description: The right candidates are out there, but the process of reaching them is unclear and time-consuming.

item2.title: New employees leave after a few weeks or months.
item2.description: People join and leave within weeks, before they have had the chance to contribute.

item3.title: Onboarding is informal or improvised.
item3.description: Each new hire is welcomed differently. There is no repeatable process.

item4.title: Supervisors do not have simple tools to support new employees.
item4.description: Team leaders want to do better but are given no resources to guide them.

item5.title: Recruitment takes too much time.
item5.description: Hours spent on interviews and paperwork that could be streamlined with clearer templates.

item6.title: The company does not have a dedicated HR department, but people issues still need to be managed.
item6.description: People decisions fall to an owner, manager or whoever is available, with no playbook to follow.

item7.title: Young employees need more guidance during adaptation.
item7.description: Young new hires need additional support to successfully adapt to the workplace.

item8.title: Job expectations are not always clear.
item8.description: Without a clear job description and expectations, employees do not know what is required of them.

pains.badge: The HR Toolkit Programme can help
pains.insightText: Small changes in onboarding reduce early turnover by up to 50% within the first 90 days.

receive.heading: What your company
receive.subhead: Participating SMEs will receive access to a practical HR Toolkit, recruitment templates, structured workshops and mentoring support.
receive.footer: Simple tools. Practical learning. Implementation support.

item1.title: Practical HR Toolkit
item1.description: A structured set of tools and templates ready to put to work from day one.

item2.title: Recruitment templates and vacancy clarification tools
item2.description: Ready-to-use job description formats and tools to clarify role requirements.

item3.title: Structured interview guides and candidate evaluation forms
item3.description: Question guides and scoring sheets that make candidate comparison consistent and objective.

item4.title: Onboarding checklists and first-day / first-week guidance
item4.description: Step-by-step lists and practical guidance for a confident start for every new hire.

item5.title: 30–60–90 day onboarding plan and supervisor guidance
item5.description: A structured adaptation roadmap and simple reference materials for supervisors.

item6.title: Adaptation meeting templates
item6.description: Ready-to-use meeting formats for the adaptation period to support new employees in a structured way.

item7.title: Feedback conversation tools and early retention risk checklists
item7.description: Feedback conversation formats and early indicators to identify and address retention risks.

item8.title: Practical workshops
item8.description: Applied, facilitated sessions on recruitment, onboarding and retention of employees.

item9.title: Mentoring circles and peer learning
item9.description: Small-group mentoring sessions and peer learning with other SMEs across the region.

map.heading: Who
map.subhead: Small and medium-sized enterprises from six selected regions of Moldova. The criteria are straightforward.
map.criteriaPrefix: The programme is especially relevant for companies that:
map.criteria1: Employ or are willing to employ young people
map.criteria2: Have current or planned hiring needs
map.criteria3: Want to improve recruitment and onboarding practices
map.criteria4: Are open to using practical HR tools
map.criteria5: Can designate a contact person for the programme
map.criteria6: Face early turnover or adaptation challenges
map.criteria7: Do not have a dedicated HR department
map.disclaimer: Submitting an expression of interest does not automatically guarantee participation. Final selection will consider eligibility, regional balance, relevance to youth employment, company motivation and readiness to participate in programme activities.

howItWorks.heading: How the programme
howItWorks.subheading: From expression of interest to practical implementation
howItWorks.subhead: Six steps. Practical support, step by step.

step1.title: Express interest
step1.description: Your company submits a short expression of interest form.

step2.title: Selection and confirmation
step2.description: Eligible SMEs are reviewed and selected based on programme criteria and regional balance.

step3.title: Baseline assessment
step3.description: The project team conducts a practical assessment of current recruitment, onboarding and retention practices.

step4.title: Toolkit and workshops
step4.description: Participating SMEs receive practical tools and join applied workshops focused on recruitment, onboarding and retention.

step5.title: Mentoring support
step5.description: Companies participate in mentoring and peer-learning activities to discuss real implementation challenges.

step6.title: Practical implementation
step6.description: SMEs adapt and use selected tools in their own company context.

howItWorks.footer: Practical support for small and medium-sized enterprises at every stage.

notAbout.heading: What the programme is
notAbout.subhead: Clear expectations from the beginning. These boundaries exist so companies know exactly what they are joining.
notAbout.item5: A guarantee that candidates will be provided
notAbout.item8: A programme only for companies with HR departments
notAbout.restatement: It is a practical support programme for SMEs that want to improve recruitment, onboarding and early retention in a realistic and manageable way.

faq.heading: Frequently
faq.a1: Participation conditions will be confirmed in the official invitation and registration information.
faq.q2: Does my company need to have an HR department?
faq.a2: No. The programme is specifically designed for SMEs that may not have dedicated HR departments.
faq.q3: Will the programme provide employees or candidates?
faq.a3: No. The programme is not a recruitment service. It helps companies improve how they recruit, onboard and retain employees.
faq.q4: Can we apply if we do not have current vacancies?
faq.a4: Yes, if your company is planning to hire or wants to improve recruitment, onboarding and retention practices.
faq.q5: How much time will participation require?
faq.a5: Participating SMEs should be ready to complete a short baseline assessment, attend practical workshops and take part in mentoring or implementation support activities.
faq.q6: Who should participate from the company?
faq.a6: The best participants are owners, directors, managers, supervisors or people responsible for recruitment, onboarding or employee management.
faq.a7: Yes. Information will be used for project purposes and reporting in aggregated form. Individual company information will not be publicly disclosed without prior agreement.
faq.q8: What happens after we submit the expression of interest?
faq.a8: The project team will review submitted forms and contact eligible companies with the next steps.
faq.footerNote: If your question is not answered here, contact the programme team directly.

cta.heading: Interested in
cta.body: Submit your expression of interest and our team will contact you with the next steps.
cta.note: Places are limited to 50 SMEs from Bălți, Chișinău, Edineț, Orhei, Soroca and Ungheni.

confidentiality.heading: Confidentiality and use of information
confidentiality.para1: Participation in the HR Toolkit Programme is entirely voluntary. Companies may withdraw at any stage without consequences.
confidentiality.para2: Information provided by companies will be used only for programme selection, baseline assessment, implementation support and reporting in aggregated form. Individual company information will not be publicly disclosed without prior agreement.
confidentiality.para3: Aggregate findings may be used to inform future programme design and policy discussions, in a form that does not identify individual companies or employees.
